newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares shoot ahead on weak U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares shoot ahead on weak U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Swiss blue chip shares closed above 3,800 points on Friday, propelled higher by weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data in September that eased fears U.S. interest rates might soon rise.

The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares added 30.4 points, or 0.81 percent, to 3,802.0 points. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) firmed 16.69 points, or 0.69 percent, to 2,431.91 points.
One dealer said the all-time SMI high of 3,813 points may be challenged next week. Purchases of futures and financial stocks after the U.S. job data helped the market, another trader noted.
Several shares have approached or broken through former resistance levels due to high liquidity, a dealer said.
Financials posted a strong showing. Union Bank of Switzerland bearer shares overcame resistance around 1,233 francs, gaining 23 to 1,239.
Among insurers, Swiss Re, which started out on a weaker note, added 14 francs to 1,346. Winterthur and Zurich also firmed.
Roche stood out among industrials, gaining 100 francs, or 1.06 percent, to 9,560. Ciba and Sandoz also gained ground.
Sulzer were down on profit taking. The shares lost seven francs to 742. Nestle recovered from the day's lows but still ended down four francs at 1,391.
Swissair and Adia profited from analysts' recommendations, putting on 1.2 percent and 2.06 percent, respectively.
